insights.headline: Gold logs worst week since March near $3,500; silver down 15% in five sessions
insights.summary: Gold fell for a fifth straight day, trading near $3,500 an ounce on Friday after losing nearly 9% on the week — its worst weekly fall since March and its lowest since September 2025. MCX gold slid to about ₹1.22 lakh per 10 g and silver to about ₹1.48 lakh per kg, with silver down more than 15% in five sessions. Markets now price a 97.3% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8–9 meeting, while gold ETFs still drew ₹3,500 crore in October and China extended its gold-buying streak to 24 months.
points: Gold traded near $3,500 on Friday, down nearly 9% on the week — its worst week since March and lowest since September 2025.
Silver fell harder, down more than 15% in five sessions to about ₹1.48 lakh per kg on MCX.
Markets price a 97.3% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike on December 8–9 after hawkish minutes and Waller’s half-point hint.
MCX gold slid to about ₹1.22 lakh per 10 g; the rupee is set for its best monthly gain in eight years on foreign inflows.
Gold ETFs still drew ₹3,500 crore in October, and China extended its gold-buying streak to 24 months.

trending.title: A hawkish Fed reprices gold
trending.summary: Fed minutes and Waller’s half-point hint pushed December hike odds to 97%, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high and yields — the week’s main driver.

trending.title: Silver’s steeper slide
trending.summary: Silver fell more than 15% in five sessions, outpacing gold’s drop, with MCX silver near ₹1.48 lakh per kg and silver ETFs at 52-week lows.

trending.title: India feels the MCX slide
trending.summary: MCX gold near ₹1.22 lakh, 40% below its all-time high; wedding households welcome lower prices while gold-loan shares feel the pinch.

trending.title: Flows keep coming as prices fall
trending.summary: Gold ETFs drew ₹3,500 crore in October, China bought a 24th straight month and Goldman Sachs sees $4,650 by end-2027, even as funds trim exposure.

items.title: Gold Logs Worst Week Since March on Hawkish Fed, AI Selloff
items.summary: Gold fell for a fifth straight day, trading near $3,500 an ounce after losing nearly 9% on the week — its worst week since March. Silver fared worse, down more than 15% in five sessions. The slide followed hawkish Federal Reserve signals and a rout in AI stocks that spurred selling across markets, with bullion breaking below $4,000, a level many had seen as a floor.

items.title: Gold and silver prices crash as Fed rate hike fears mount
items.summary: MCX December gold traded at ₹1,22,435 per 10 g, down 3.94%, while silver fell 6% to ₹1,48,034 per kg, both at their lowest since September 2025; COMEX gold was at $3,551.90 an ounce as December Fed hike expectations topped 97% and the gold-silver ratio hit a 14-month high of 85.5:1.

items.title: Gold Price Crash Tests $3,500 as Fed Hike Bets Reach 97%
items.summary: Gold tested the $3,500 level, touching an overnight low of $3,514.50, as markets priced a 97.3% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8-9 meeting. Spot gold traded at $3,568.65, heading for a weekly loss of about 9%, its steepest in eight months, while silver fell 14% on the week to $42.15.

items.title: Gold Sinks To One-Year Low, Silver Plunges Rs 2.46 lakh From Record High
items.summary: Delhi gold of 99.9% purity fell Rs 5,200 to Rs 1,29,300 per 10 g on Friday, its lowest in a year, while silver dropped Rs 4,000 to Rs 1.58 lakh per kg — Rs 2.46 lakh below its January record of Rs 4.04 lakh; spot gold slid to $3,515 an ounce.

items.title: Gold Hits 15-Month Low, Silver Drops Near Rs 1.48 Lakh | Three Reasons Why Precious Metals Are Crashing?
items.summary: MCX gold fell 3.84% to Rs 1,22,561 per 10 g and silver slid 5.99% to Rs 1,48,050 per kg, NDTV Profit reported, as both metals hit 15-month lows. Gold has lost Rs 4,891 per 10 g and silver Rs 9,432 per kg in the session.

items.title: Gold price crash: Yellow metal and silver slump over 4% each on MCX
items.summary: Gold fell nearly 4% to about Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g on MCX and silver slid nearly 6% to Rs 1.48 lakh per kg as the sell-off deepened, CNBC-TV18 reported. A strengthening dollar and rising expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike drove the slide, with spot gold at $3,551.68, down 8.9% on the week.

items.title: Gold set for worst week in eight months as firm dollar, Fed hike bets weigh
items.summary: Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,551.68 by 0257 GMT, down about 8.9% on the week — its sharpest weekly fall since March — as a dollar near a 19-month high and a 97.3% chance of a December Fed hike weighed on bullion. Silver fell 2% to $41.90 an ounce, and Swiss gold exports fell 34% in October.

items.title: MCX Gold Sinks 40% From All-Time High: Analysts Flag The One Level Traders Must Watch
items.summary: MCX gold December futures fell 2.03% to Rs 1,22,659 per 10 g on Friday, with silver down 4.96% to Rs 1,49,673 per kg, and NDTV Profit reports gold is now over 40% below its all-time high after a fifth straight losing session; analysts cited in the piece watch $3,500 an ounce as the key support for spot gold.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD) & Silver Price Forecast: Gold Heads for Worst Week in Eight Months, Can $3,518 Hold?
items.summary: Spot gold traded near $3,551.68 an ounce after touching its lowest since September 2025, heading for its worst week in eight months. CME FedWatch showed a 93.9% chance of a quarter-point December hike. Gold is testing $3,518 support and turns bearish below the $3,597 pivot, while silver traded near $41.46 with RSI near 15.

items.title: Gold under a hiking Fed: central-bank demand versus real rates
items.summary: Kitco's commentary argues real yields, not the dollar alone, are driving gold's slide, with December hike odds near 96% and the 10-year real yield near 2.9%; central banks bought 321 tonnes in the third quarter, 42% more than a year earlier, but that buying runs on a slower clock than the rates market.

items.title: Gold Price Outlook: Goldman Sachs Sees Gold At $4,650 By 2027-End; Central Bank Buying To Drive
items.summary: Goldman Sachs sees gold reaching $4,650 an ounce by the end of 2027, with continued central-bank buying driving the recovery. The call comes even as gold trades near 14-month lows under pressure from expectations of further US rate hikes.

items.title: Gold ETFs attract ₹3,500 crore despite price correction: Should you increase your allocation?
items.summary: Gold ETFs drew ₹3,500 crore in October, the fifth straight month of net inflows, according to the World Gold Council, with an estimated ₹2,450 crore more in November 1–11; holdings rose to 126 tonnes even as gold ETF prices fell about 5% on Friday.

items.title: Rupee set for best monthly gain in 8 years on strong foreign fund inflows
items.summary: The rupee has gained 2.46% so far in November to 92.68 per dollar, its best monthly rise in eight years, helped by nearly $13 billion in foreign inflows, lower crude prices and exporter dollar sales. It rose 0.67% on Friday, crossing 93 for the first time since April.

items.title: Gold, silver fall to 2026 lows; experts say volatility likely to persist
items.summary: Gold fell about 4% to Rs 1,22,435 per 10 g and silver 6% to Rs 1,48,034 per kg, the lowest of 2026. Kotak NEO's Anindya Banerjee noted the dollar index near 104, a 19-month high, with a December Fed hike almost fully priced in, while Aspect Bullion's Darshan Desai said retail buyers stayed cautious, preferring smaller staggered purchases.

items.title: Gold price crash: Muthoot Finance, Manappuram shares lose sheen, down up to 5% | Is gold heading for deeper correction?
items.summary: Shares of gold-loan firms Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance fell up to 5% as bullion slid to a one-year low, with Muthoot down 3% to an intraday low of Rs 2,480. Cheaper gold shrinks the value of pledged jewellery backing their loans, raising concern over loan-to-value buffers and slower disbursements if the slide continues.

items.title: 18K gold slips below Rs 1 lakh, down 8% in three days: Is it a buying opportunity?
items.summary: IBJA 18K gold has stayed below Rs 1 lakh per 10 g for three straight sessions, falling 8.06% to Rs 92,688 from Rs 1,00,814 on November 17, as a stronger dollar, higher bond yields and Fed tightening bets pressured bullion. IBJA put 24K gold at Rs 1,23,584 and 22K at Rs 1,13,203 per 10 g.

items.title: GJC alerts BIS over suspected gold adulteration, urges jewellers to tighten quality checks
items.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council has alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards over reports of rhenium- and iridium-based alloys being used to add weight to gold jewellery without matching purity. GJC said BIS is taking the matter seriously, urged jewellers to tighten quality checks, and asked buyers to verify hallmarks on the BIS Care app and insist on GST-paid invoices.

items.title: Gold, silver prices near a bottom? JM Financial, Motilal Oswal flag key levels for a rebound
items.summary: JM Financial puts MCX gold support near ₹1,20,000, with rebound targets of ₹1,36,500 and ₹1,45,000, and silver support at ₹1,50,000; Motilal Oswal sees a medium-term floor of $3,400–$3,450 an ounce for gold and about $40 for silver.

items.title: Gold ETFs down 5%; Silver ETFs plunge over 6%, trade at 52-week lows
items.summary: Gold ETFs fell 5% and silver ETFs plunged over 6% to 52-week lows, Business Standard reported, as bullion prices crashed. Gold futures traded up to 4% lower around $3,530 and silver futures near $41.60, down nearly 6%, on fears of a December Fed rate hike, a stronger dollar and rising bond yields.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall to over three month low of $705 billion
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell more than $14 billion in the week to November 13 to $705.3 billion, the lowest in about three months, RBI data showed, with foreign currency assets down $7.8 billion and the value of the central bank's gold holdings down $6.1 billion. The rupee strengthened on Friday to 92.67 per dollar, its strongest since April.

items.title: Gold miners face new test after years of exceptional profits
items.summary: Gold miners face an earnings test as falling prices squeeze margins after almost two years in which higher prices offset rising costs, with JSE-listed producers falling sharply. Analysts say downgrades are possible if costs keep rising while realised prices fall, though strong cash flows leave balance sheets able to withstand weaker prices for now.

items.title: Metals Sell-Off Runs Ahead of Physical Markets
items.summary: ING argues the metals sell-off looks more like a sharp unwind of bullish investor positions than weakening physical demand: gold is down about 9% on the week in its steepest weekly fall since March, while physical copper in China stays tight, with Shanghai stocks at their lowest since late 2023 and the Yangshan premium at a record $500 a tonne.

items.title: China Extends Gold-Buying Streak to 24 Months as Beijing Bucks the Price Slump
items.summary: China's central bank added 26 tonnes of gold in October, its 24th consecutive month of buying, lifting reserves to 2,435 tonnes, while central banks bought 675 tonnes in January-September. Goldman Sachs cut its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650 an ounce from $4,800.

items.title: Festive gold sales value jumps 15-25 pc despite high prices: WGC
items.summary: Festive gold sales value rose 15-25% year-on-year over Dhanteras-Diwali, the World Gold Council said, while volumes were largely flat to slightly higher as average festive prices ran nearly 10% above last year. October gold imports were $5.51 billion, more than triple September's but 63% lower than a year earlier.

items.title: Householders With Weddings Relieved As Gold, Silver Prices Slide
items.summary: Families in Telangana with weddings ahead welcomed the slide after months of record prices, with many who had postponed jewellery purchases now willing to buy, while bullion traders worry about the falling value of their stocks; the paper attributes the drop largely to developments in international markets.
